articles.text: MǓQIN: Xiǎo Míng, nǐ zài chī yìdiǎnr a.
MOTHER: Xiǎo Míng, have some more to eat.
XIǍO MÍNG: Mā, wǒ chībǎo le, bù xiǎng chī le.
XIǍO MÍNG: I'm full, Mom. I don't want any more.
MǓQIN: Měitian niàn shū niànde zhème wǎn, zài bù duō chī yìdiǎnr, zěnme xíng na?
MOTHER: You study so late every day; if you keep eating so little, how will that do?
XIǍO MÍNG: Wǒ zhēnde chībǎo le, yìdiǎnr dōu bù xiǎng chī le.
XIǍO MÍNG: I've really had enough. I just don't want any more.
MǓQIN: Háizi, nǐ yǒu shénme xīnshì? Kě bu kěyi hé wo tántan?
MOTHER: Son, what do you have on your mind? Can you talk about it with me?
XIǍO MÍNG: Mā, nǐ zuòxia. Zánmen lái Měiguo sìwǔnián le. Láide shíhou wǒ hái shi ge háizi, xiànzài yǐjing shi dàren le. Wǒ suīrán zhǎngdà le, kěshi zuò shénme shìr, háishi xiǎng xiān hé nín tántan.

XIǍO MÍNG: Mom, sit down. We've been in America for four or five years now. When we came I was still a child, but now I'm an adult. But even though I've grown up, whenever I do something I still like to discuss it with you first.
MǓQIN: Hǎode, yǒu shénme shìr, nǐ jiù shuō ba!
MOTHER: Okay, if you have something you'd like to talk about, go ahead.
XIǍO MÍNG: Mā, wǒ yǒu jǐge Měiguo tóngxué, dōu shi xué Zhōngwénde. Jīnnián shǔjià, tāmen xiǎng dào Yàzhōu qù kànkan, wǒ yě xiǎng hé tāmen yìqǐ qù.
XIǍO MÍNG: Mom, I have a few American classmates who study Chinese. This summer vacation, they want to go to Asia, and I'd like to go with them.
MǓQIN: Dōu shi niánqīng rén ma?
MOTHER: Are they all young people?
XIǍO MÍNG: Shì a, dōu shi dàxuéshēng.
XIǍO MÍNG: Yes, they're all college students.
MǓQIN: Tāmen qù Yàzhōu, shi qù wánr háishi qù yánjiū Yàzhōude zhèngzhì, wénhuà qíngxing?
MOTHER: Are they going to Asia for fun or to study the political and cultural situation in Asia?
XIǍO MÍNG: Wǒ xiǎng, tāmen juéde Yàzhōu wénhuà hěn yǒu yìsi, Yàzhōu gèguó shèhuìde qíngkuàng yě hěn yǒu yìsi.
XIǍO MÍNG: I think they find Asian culture and the social situation in the Asian countries very interesting.
MǓQIN: Tāmen juéde zuì yǒu yìside dìfang shi nǎr a?
MOTHER: Which place do they think is the most interesting?
XIǍO MÍNG: Dāngrán shi Zhōngguó!
XIǍO MÍNG: China, of course!
MǓQIN: Nǐ líkāi Zhōngguo zhǐ yǒu sìwǔnián, jiù xiǎng huíqu le?
MOTHER: You left China only four or five years ago, and already you want to go back again?
XIǍO MÍNG: Wǒ láide shíhou cái shàng gāozhōng, duì Zhōngguo wénhuà dǒngdéde tài shǎo. Wǒ xiǎng wǒ yīnggāi huíqu kànkan.
XIǍO MÍNG: When I came I was only in senior high, and I understood too little about Chinese culture. I think I ought to go back to visit.

MǓQIN: Zhōngguóde wénhuà yǐjing yǒu sìqiānniánde lìshǐ, yǒu yìside dōngxi hěn duō. Nǐ yào yánjiū Zhōngguo wénhuà, wǒ bù fǎnduì. Búguò, zǒu yǐqián, nǐ yídìng yào hé Yéye hǎohāor tán yícì. Tā jǐshínián méiyou huíqu le, yídìng yǒu hěn duō huà yào hé nǐ shuō.

MOTHER: Chinese culture already has four thousand years of history, and there are many interesting things. I'm not against your wanting to study Chinese culture. But before you go you have to talk it over thoroughly with Grandpa. He hasn't been back in several decades and I'm sure he'll have a lot to say to you.
XIǍO MÍNG: Wǒ jìzhu le, yídìng hé Yéye hǎohāor tányitán.
XIǍO MÍNG: I'll remember. I'll make sure I talk it over thoroughly with Grandpa.
